Six well-specified overreach conclusions covering substrate, pathway, catalytic details, template use and evolutionary history, plus external evidence needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Release, hierarchy, Pfam comments, homology record and member proteins for all three families are supported by the bundle. Superfamily correctly read as positive claim of common ancestry; fold-only superfamilies neither homologous nor declared convergent; separate families explained. Rejects transferring conjugation, Ras/Rap effector binding and p97 N-domain binding by name, with within-family and fold-only caveats; clearly separates background biology from SCOPe records and states that no quality checks were run.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families, sunids, representative domains (d3chya_, d1orda1 1-107, d1r8ja2 2-135) with their annotations, freeze date, sibling c.23 superfamilies, all supported by bundle. Superfamily identified as the deepest shared homology-bearing node; fold sharing explicitly not the basis; separate superfamilies not evidence of convergence. Rejects phospho-receiver signaling, KaiA clock attribution to the N-domain, catalysis/PLP transfer, and template interchange; correctly treats ligand comments as entry-specific and SPACI/AEROSPACI as quality, not evolutionary, measures. Literature vs SCOPe sources clearly separated.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Hierarchy, sibling sunids, release metadata, homology scope, d1vdza2 boundaries and 1vdz domain split all bundle-supported. Reasoning complete: positive ancestry claim within b.84.5 (one family, V1 and A1), fold-level only against b.84.1-b.84.4, explicitly not a claim of convergence, class purely architectural; function/template/F1 limits and absence of quality data stated. However the claim that 2.05 returned 404 and the superfamily first appears in 2.06/2.07 is an API-dependent release-history assertion with no supporting response in the bundle.

Complete and fully supported, including empty inconsistency lists, family contents, Pfam xref, and homology warning. Correct fold-vs-superfamily inference, treats f.21.3 possible-link note as a hypothesis, explicitly declines to conclude unrelated or remotely homologous without external evidence, limits transfer, and names structural alignment, profile/HMM, and literature evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correctly places c.2.1.1/c.2.1.8/c.2.1.9 as sister families under c.2.1 with sunids, homology records and the 'N-terminal all-beta domain defines family' comment, all matching the evidence bundle. Interprets superfamily as probable remote common ancestry, separate families as divergent lineages, and explicitly bars transfer of ligand (NAD/NADP/CoA), mechanism, zinc, oligomer and gating. Notes fold alone is not ancestry evidence and that mechanistic statements come from general knowledge. One muddled sentence about 'family is the deepest level they share' is not materially wrong. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage and identifiers, cites the family 100905 'not a true family' annotation and explains the curated comment overrides the generic homology_implied_by_level=true flag (supported by bundle). Calibrated: structural/design similarity only, explicitly does not claim they are unrelated, rejects function/ion transfer, recommends excluding the pair from homology benchmarks.

Complete and fully bundle-supported: 1.69 lineages with sunids (c.137.1.1 vs c.23.14.1), 2.08 d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1 (1-118) c.23.14.2 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1, tag domains, superfamily rename, first visible in 1.71 and stable through 1.73/1.75. Inference complete and well supported: artifact lineage with sunids, homology endpoint warning cited, d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1, tag similarity rejected, class-l levels as bookkeeping, benchmark/masking advice. One noncentral error: speculates from memory that the 8 residues fit a FLAG-type DYKDDDDK tag; actual residues are QVQLQQSG. Explicitly flagged as unchecked, so a minor imprecision rather than a central fault. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

Correct and complete: single d1acca_ (43828, f.11.1.1) in 1.75 and 2.01-2.03, two domains from 2.04 through 2.08 with correct sids, sunids, boundaries, sccs and lineage names. Interprets the split as recognition of a reusable PA14 module sharing a superfamily with GLEYA, GH31 and beta-glucosidase PA14 domains, while stating that different classes and folds mean no homology claim rather than proof of unrelatedness, and that superfamily membership transfers ancestry but not pore formation, receptor binding or carbohydrate binding. Search guidance is per-domain, coverage-aware and release-pinned, and it notes that absence of warnings is not positive evidence.

All must_include met; identifiers, boundaries, sccs, sibling families, annotation comments and homology records all bundle-supported. Strong interpretation: four ancient superfamily modules plus novel N-terminal fold, no catalytic transfer, different superfamilies not evidence of separate origin, literature origin flagged. Factual slip: states each domain sits in a different class, but a1 (c.55) and a2 (c.52) are both class c. Noncentral. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: correct lineage and sunids, lengths, both domain comments, the 're' flag with definition and the note that the repeat representative d4cj9a_ lacks it, and the repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 with coordinates applying only to that domain. Interprets 're' as a curatorial heterogeneity convention rather than an error, warns that whole-domain identity/RMSD/coverage cannot test homology here, recommends per-repeat comparison and stratifying 're' families in benchmarks, and rejects function/host-role transfer. Clearly separates retrieved records from background structural knowledge. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Correct, supported metadata. Cites stable 2.08 selector for reproducibility, says periodic update does not supersede stable, records full dated label plus retrieval date if periodic data used, and warns against citing only 'current'. Periodic semantics: dated update on 2.08 base adding newly deposited PDB entries mostly by automated classification, a moving snapshot rather than frozen release. Limits stated. Complete.

Complete: shared a.47.2.1 lineage; fragment comment and 'ms' flag with 1.55/1.75/2.08 annotation history; d1dn1b_ curated (17771) then absent in 2.01 and back as automated match (302344) to curated d3c98b_ from 2.06; fold defined by four long helices so fragments' three-helix structure (spectrin-like) cannot show the fold and the label is inherited by sequence identity. Correct handling of spectrin resemblance (neither homology nor non-homology), level-specific homology claims, no function transfer, full domain as reference with curation caveat, release pinning. Honest about not establishing why d1dn1b_ was dropped/re-added (obsolescence not retrieved) and not retrieving quality records. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Covers all must_include items: convergence across lineages (TIM barrel c.1.7, DHFR c.71.1 vs Rossmann c.2), divergence within c.2.1 backed by the homology endpoint, and an integrated evidence standard (sequence/HMM, global structural alignment with topology, motifs in equivalent context, domain architecture, phylogeny). All sunids, family list (13 children incl. c.2.1.0), fold core descriptions, c.2 curator comment, and release/periodic-update labels are supported by the bundle. Neither must_avoid violated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Body is accurate and well sourced: 2.04 lineages for both domains with b.23.2 and b.18.1 named, move localized to 2.05, 2.08 shared superfamily with families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 distinct, family comment citing PubMed 17977833 quoted correctly, and structure-comparison values attributed to cluster representative 1nqjA with an explicit warning that they are not results for 1nqdA. Good critical handling: notes similar-strength hits from other folds so the comparison alone does not single out b.18.1, and notes absence of homology warnings is not positive evidence. Limits section properly blocks ligand, Ca-site, specificity and template transfer. Decisive flaw is the headline summary 'A shared fold is now a shared superfamily', which misstates the 2.04 relationship as fold-level; the next paragraph contradicts it by stating the domains were in different folds and shared only class b. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.
